result.title: E5 PRE-SPIKE TAPE (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1): accumulation, re-base and contraction detectors that fire WITHOUT a big up day, in IDX, US and crypto, with the KOD VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET definition as the frozen reference member
result.angle: NEW TAPE FAMILY: a tape-only detector family whose members require the ABSENCE of a move on the signal day (quiet band, not repriced) and read multi-session volume structure, post-fade path structure, or volatility contraction, instead of the day return / ARA lock / breakout / volume-surge-with-return triggers that every E1 (F1..F10) and E2 (G1..G11) member uses.
result.thesis: Every detector this lab has validated (F1_ARA, G2_RET30, the E3 plan grid, the E4 shorts, US_BREAKOUT_v1) triggers on the signal day's own return, so detection is real (9.3x/5.4x/4.6x matched random) but the executable edge is negative because entry comes inside a move whose median next-5-session path is -10% (E1/E2 REPORT.md; r5_median -10.3% US, -11.5% crypto). The hypothesis: a subset of future +30% moves is preceded, in daily bars, by a tape structure that is informative WITHOUT a return: (A) a multi-session volume creep (median volume of the last 5 sessions >= 1.5x the median of the prior 20) while price stays inside its own noise band and is not yet repriced (ret20 < +30%), the pre-markup accumulation signature of an operator working a thin IDX float ('goreng') or of informed buying ahead of a catalyst in US/crypto; (B) a re-base 6-40 sessions after a faded +30% day, where price gave back at least half the spike-to-peak gain but has held above the pre-spike level for five sessions in a quiet band (the holders left after the fade are sticky, so a second leg needs less supply); (C) a volatility contraction (10-session vol <= half of 60-session vol) in a historically volatile name that has not collapsed (supply exhausted before expansion). The mechanism that would make it true is that coordinated or informed buying shows in volume and path structure before it shows in price. The harness's v2 matched controls remove the price state (volatility tercile, momentum tercile, drawdown tercile, liquidity, price band, market cap, listing age), so a positive result is attributable to the volume/path structure and not to the already-known fact that volatile, beaten-down names reprice more often (vol20 AUC 0.68/0.78/0.56, dd60 0.40/0.25/0.41). The reference member A1_CREEP_QUIET is the KOD-DET-v0 VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET tape definition exactly as frozen on 2026-10-08 in kod-machine/research/ZEALAND_PILOT_v1/01_protocol/protocol.json and 03_card/price_facts.py (creep = median vol t-4..t / median vol t-24..t-5 >= 1.5; quiet = median rngr over t-4..t <= 1.0 and |ret5| <= 2*vol20*sqrt(5); not repriced = ret20 < 0.30), so its thresholds were fixed before this experiment for a different purpose and have never been tuned on any moonshot outcome; running it through the harness gives the KOD doctrine the population base rate and non-events (doctrine lines 79-81) it has never had for that detector (one retrospective case, NO_SIGNAL).
result.why_not_already_falsified: Signal family: all 21 frozen E1/E2 members need a move on the signal day (ret1 >= 3..30%, ARA lock, close above the 60-session high, open gap >= 10% held, 5-session return >= 30%) or a single-day volume surge (G4_VOL10 at 10x, G3/G5/G11 with a return or vol20 condition); none has a quiet condition, none uses a 5-session volume median against a prior-20 median, none excludes repriced names, none reads the post-spike path 6-40 sessions later, none measures vol10/vol60 contraction. A4_RVOL_FLAT explicitly requires |ret1| <= vol20 and no 60-session breakout, the opposite of G6/brk60. Information source: E1/E2's weak-signal tables (research/E1/discovery/signal_stats.csv; research/E2/REPORT.md) measured SINGLE-DAY ratios at the session before an episode start (volr 0.50, valr 0.50, freqr 0.50, rngr 0.49) and never computed the 5-session creep, the quiet band, the re-base path or the contraction on any panel, so 'volume surges carry no information on the start day' does not test multi-session accumulation that may precede the move by 1-20 sessions. Structure: E3 (108 plans) and E4 (144+288 short plans) searched execution plans for the SAME big-day detectors; US_BREAKOUT_v1 is a move trigger (close > prior 60-session closing high); E4 shorted the fade within 5 sessions of the spike while B1/B2 fire only after the fade has completed and price has re-based, a state no experiment has looked at. The volatility finding (the only pre-event separator) is used only as a conditioning tercile in A3/C1 and is neutralised by the matched controls, so the test asks what the structure adds beyond it. Unknown (not falsified, not confirmed): whether any member reaches 200 flags with E30 lift, whether the flagged population has the negative drift of the moonshot-prone names, whether a 5/10/20-session hold captures a move that arrives later; nothing in the repo answers these, which is why the experiment is needed.

protocol.family: MOONSHOT_E5 family, idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py, VERSION v1, long only, 8 members in three mechanism groups, thresholds fixed in protocol.json before any flag is computed. Common features (column d uses sessions <= d only; all from RULE_FIELDS close/prev/high/low/volume/present/tradeable/open): ret1 = close/prev-1 on tradeable sessions with prev>0; level = reference chain exp(cumsum log(close/prev)) as moonshot_g; ret5/ret20 on level; logret for vol; vol20 = std of logret over d-19..d (min 15), vol10 over d-9..d (min 8), vol60 over d-59..d (min 40); rng = (high-low)/prev where high/low present; rngr = rng / median(rng over d-20..d-1) (min 10); rngr5 = median(rngr over d-4..d) (5 values required); v5 = median(volume over d-4..d) on present sessions (untraded = 0), v_base = median(volume over d-24..d-5) (min 15 present), creep = v5/v_base where v_base>0; volr = volume/median(volume d-20..d-1) as moonshot_g; brk60 = level > max level over d-60..d-1 (min 20); dd60 = level/max level over d-59..d - 1; quiet(d) = rngr5 <= 1.0 and |ret5| <= 2*vol20*sqrt(5) [KOD price_quiet_vs_own_range verbatim]; not_repriced(d) = ret20 < 0.30 [KOD price_already_repriced = false]; hivol20(d) = vol20 >= 67th percentile of vol20 across evaluable names at d (cross-section at d only, as E1 uses the cross-sectional median); hivol60(d) likewise on vol60. Rules must pass rules/audit.py (numpy/pandas only, literal module constants) and the prefix-first LookaheadError check (all windows trailing).
detectors: A1_CREEP_QUIET: creep >= 1.5 and quiet and not_repriced (KOD-DET-v0 VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET tape facts, thresholds frozen 2026-10-08; the protocol's reference detector)
A2_CREEP2_QUIET: creep >= 2.0 and quiet and not_repriced
A3_CREEP_QUIET_HIVOL: A1 and hivol20 (the only known pre-event separator as a conditioning tercile; neutralised by the matched controls' volatility tercile so the matched test isolates the creep)
A4_RVOL_FLAT: volr >= 3 and |ret1| <= vol20 and not brk60 and not_repriced (a single-session volume-without-price day that is not a breakout)

B1_REBASE: there is a session s0 in [d-40, d-6] with ret1(s0) >= 0.30 (take the most recent); pre = level(s0-1); peak = max level over [s0, d-1]; level(d) <= pre + 0.5*(peak-pre) (at least half the spike-to-peak gain given back); min level over [d-4, d] >= pre (held above the pre-spike level for 5 sessions); quiet(d)
C1_CONTRACT: vol10 <= 0.5*vol60 and hivol60 and dd60 >= -0.5 and not_repriced (contraction in a historically volatile name that has not collapsed)
protocol.plans: Primary grid per detector: entry fixed with entry_lag 1 (IDX: next close, as E1/E3; US/CRYPTO: next open, as E2/E4) x exit fixed x holding_days {5, 10, 20} = 3 plans (24 (detector, plan) pairs per market, 72 harness runs in all; every run reported in <market>/discovery/plans.csv). Optional second exit stop_ref (sell at the first close in entry+1..entry+h-1 at or below the signal session's reference close) is included for every market only if the experiment runs on a tree that expresses close-referenced exits for open-entry markets (origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side generalises conditional rules; HEAD execution.py:365-366 restricts them to close entries, i.e. IDX); the protocol records at freeze which of 3 or 6 plans applies per market, before any number. holding_days 10 and 20 are new to the lab and are there because an accumulation signal need not resolve within 5 sessions; overlap 'skip' per name applies (backtest.py:302-316). No conditional entries (there is no move to confirm or pull back from). Reference row per market: A1_CREEP_QUIET|fixed1|fixed|h5, reported beside the grid as the population test of the KOD tape detector.
protocol.discovery_period: IDX 2021-01-22..2022-12-30 (TIER_1, panel-20261013T194245Z rebuilt from the pinned mirror commit, registry ca_registry-20261013T194256Z, as E3); US and CRYPTO 2020-07-01..2022-12-31 (US: panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z, causal-close-v2 with unit_factor, 4,878 names, read_through 2023-12-29; CRYPTO: panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z, 683 pairs incl. delisted). Per-year admissibility uses calendar years 2021, 2022 (IDX) and 2020 (from July), 2021, 2022 (US/CRYPTO).
protocol.validation_period: IDX 2023-01-02..2023-12-29; US and CRYPTO 2023-01-01..2023-12-31; one recorded harness run per market of the frozen pair (write_run -> results/runs, RUNS.jsonl) plus the detection evidence from e1.Study.evaluate on validation. Justification for re-using 2023: the outcomes seen on 2023 belong to return-triggered detectors (F1_ARA, G2_RET30, breakout) and their plans; no E5 member's flags have ever been computed on any panel, so 2023 is out-of-sample for this family; the only leakage is knowledge of the 2023 base rates and of big-day behaviour, declared in the protocol, and the protocol bans any E5 computation on 2023 before SELECTED is committed. The holdouts (IDX 2024-01-02..2025-02-21; US/CRYPTO 2024-01-01 on) are never loaded: the Study ends its market at the last validation session (e1.py:105-107) and every RunConfig sets end explicitly (on HEAD there is no GLOBAL_HOLDOUT code guard for US/CRYPTO; merging PR #7 first adds it). The prospective paper ledger is the forward arm if a pair validates (new POLICY_ID, not a change to PAPER-POLICY-v4).
protocol.admissibility: Discovery, per market, two gates both pre-registered. Detection gate per detector (E1 detector_table rule, e1.py:306-323, on the family module): flags >= 200 and E30 Wilson 95% lower bound > the period base rate; evaluate() also reports lift vs 200 matched random draws per flag and the one-sided p (floor 0.005), recall, median lead, r5_median vs matched. Trading gate per (detector, plan) (E3 rule, e3.py:99-115, applied verbatim): scored >= 200; average net return > 0 after fees/tiers; above the matched-random distribution with one-sided p < 0.05 (200 draws, floor 0.005); average net return > 0 in every discovery calendar year with >= 50 scored. Selection: among pairs whose detector passes the detection gate AND whose plan passes the trading gate, the highest average net return; ties by scored trades, then grid order (e3.select); at most one pair per market; none admissible = SELECTED stays None for that market and MOONSHOT_E5_<market>_D1 is never created. Freeze: the selected (detector, entry_rule, entry_window, exit_rule, holding_days) per market is written into moonshot_e5.SELECTED and committed (Rule.plan, rule hash covers it) before any validation number. Validation pass per market: scored >= 100, average net > 0, one-sided p < 0.05 vs matched random under the same plan (E3 validation rule) AND detection p_one_sided_vs_matched < 0.05 with lift > 1 on validation (what paper.decide's detection gate reads). Reported, not judged: hit rate, median net return, fill rate and status counts, same-session random baseline, per-price-band precision, flags on consecutive sessions per name, the share of FILL-C scored IDX trades exceeding 10% of entry-session volume (CORRECTION_01 diagnostic), US results under the unit_schedule quarantine as a sensitivity, horizon-20 repricing rate (E30 at t+1..t+20) if the Study horizon parameter is added. Search size is 8 detectors + 24 pairs per market and is stated in every output.
protocol.matched_controls: Trading stage: harness controls v2 (controls.py:71-74): for each attempted signal, 200 draws on the same session from evaluable names in the same price band, liquidity quintile (20-session median traded value), market-cap quintile (IDX mirror era only), volatility tercile, momentum tercile, drawdown tercile and listing-age bucket, relaxed from the last feature until >= 5 names, executed under the identical plan, fill model, costs and lot rules; plus the same-session uniform baseline; seed 20261007 (matched seed+1). Detection stage: E1's matched pool (price band, liquidity, market cap), 200 draws per flag, seed 20261008 (e1.py:215-227, 334-355). Because volatility, momentum and drawdown terciles are matched, the A3/C1 volatility conditions and the known 'volatile, drawn-down names reprice more' effect are removed from the comparison; a pass therefore attributes to the volume/path structure.
protocol.costs_model: Per-market harness profiles unchanged (profiles.py): IDX fee 0.15% buy / 0.25% sell, lot 100, notional Rp10,000,000, max_participation 0.10, fill model C (FILL-C-v1 decision-time capacity, registry-scaled; the CORRECTION_01 limitation that C never checks the entry session is reported as a diagnostic, not corrected here), ca_mode registry (rights issues and unresolved resets exclude the trade), ARA lock refuses entry; US: $5,000 notional, fee 0 / SEC fee, price-tier cost per side 1.5% (<$1), 0.5% ($1-5), 0.15% ($5-20), 0.05% (>$20) on the as-traded price, units as_traded, fill model B (FILL-B-v1 decision-time 20-session median volume), quarantine none (every name kept; repair_v3 showed the quarantine is outcome-correlated), ca_mode adjusted; CRYPTO: $5,000, 0.1% fee + 0.1% slippage per side, fill model A (ex-post 10% of entry-session volume, as E2/E4's recorded runs, labelled), ca_mode adjusted, UTC days. No price impact, no dividends, no carry on longs, daily bars only. Precondition stage re-runs the recorded reference runs on E5's panels (IDX 20261008T000401Z or FILL-C 20261009T050040Z; CRYPTO 20261008T005732Z; US 20261008T115656Z) and records REPRODUCED/DEVIATES as E3/E4 did.

data_needed: IDX panel per manifest panel-20261013T194245Z (csv absent in this checkout; rebuild with `idxsig build-panel` from the pinned mirror manifest idx_mirror-20261013T192142Z; the on-disk panel-20261007T225823Z carries the same TIER_1 rows for discovery/validation and is the fallback) and registry ca_registry-20261013T194256Z

US repair panel panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z.csv.gz (on disk; format panel-global-v2-units; 2020-01-02..2023-12-29, unit_factor) for both the trading harness (units as_traded, fill B) and the detection Study (needs the format check relaxed)
Crypto panel panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z.csv.gz (on disk; the Study and harness end the market at 2023-12-31)

Fields used by the rules: close, prev, high, low, volume, present, tradeable, open (all RULE_FIELDS); volume is used in base units so the unverified meaning of the crypto `value` column does not matter; IDX high/low exist on 87.5% of mirror rows and 12.5% have volume 0, so quiet/creep are NaN (no flag) where undefined

No external data, no network pulls, no filings, no funding/OI; kod-machine/research/ZEALAND_PILOT_v1/01_protocol/pin/ZEAL.CO.json only as a unit-test fixture to assert the harness A1 rule reproduces price_facts.measures() (no outcome is read from it)
code_changes: idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py (new rule module, same shape as moonshot_g.py): VERSION 'v1'; FEATURE_ARGS = ('close','prev','high','low','volume','present','tradeable','open') so e1.Study._signals and paper.scan_frame can call features(*args); features() returns the moonshot_g keys (ret1, rel1, ret5, ret20, volr, brk60, dd60, cpos, gap, hold, vol20) plus creep, rngr5, quiet, vol10, vol60, hivol20, hivol60, rebase_pre_ok/rebase_retrace_ok; family_flags(f) returns the 8 members; FAMILY = 8 (name, text) tuples; SELECTED = (('IDX', None), ('US', None), ('CRYPTO', None)) frozen later per market; rules() emits E5_CAND_<market>_<name> (hold 5, plan None) while unselected and MOONSHOT_E5_<market>_D1 with Rule.plan after the freeze (pattern: moonshot_e3.rules / moonshot_e4.selected_plan). Rebase member vectorised with trailing lags only: for k in 6..40, spike_k = lag(ret1 >= 0.30, k), pre_k = lag(level, k+1), peak_k = lag(rolling_max(level, k), 1); most recent k via masked argmax; min level over d-4..d via rolling min. Cross-sectional percentile uses np.nanpercentile over column d of evaluable names (as moonshot_e1's cross-sectional median). Module imports only numpy/pandas; all module-level values literals (rules/audit.py).
idxsig/rules/__init__.py registry(): add moonshot_e5 to the module tuple (line 61-64).

idxsig/e5.py (new experiment module cloned from e4.py's market-loop structure and e3.py's helpers): protocol()/plan_grid/plan_id/plan_row/admissibility/select/selected_tuple/write_csv/write_json reused from e3; harness_config(proto, market, rule_id, period, plan) builds RunConfig from protocol['markets'][market] (panel_manifest, registry_manifest for IDX, notional, fees, fill_model, units, quarantine, ca_mode) with explicit start/end; stages run_reproduce (precondition runs per market, REPRODUCED/DEVIATES on record), run_discovery (per market: detection table via e1.Study(df, meta, protocol_path=E5 protocol, profile=PROFILES[market], family_module=moonshot_e5).detector_table('discovery') + evaluate() per member -> <market>/discovery/detector_selection.csv; trading grid through backtest.run with signal_cache -> plans.csv, reference_summary.json, selected_summary.json, summary.json with selected_tuple and freeze instruction), run_validation (requires moonshot_e5.selected(market) == discovery selected_tuple; write_run-recorded harness run; detection.json from Study.evaluate(detector, 'validation'); result.json with passed and consequence). _stamp records protocol sha256, panel sha, registry sha, detector module sha, code_state, exactly as e3._stamp.

idxsig/e1.py small generalisations: (a) accept panel format 'panel-global-v2-units' for US (line 100-102 currently expects 'panel-global-v1'); (b) guard the IGNITION benchmark lookup at line 190 (`sig['ign']` = NaN when the family has no IGNITION member) so Study works with a family that has none; (c) optional HORIZON parameter on Study (default 5) to report the horizon-20 repricing rate as a secondary statistic; existing E1/E2 behaviour unchanged (defaults) and covered by the existing tests.

idxsig/cli.py: subcommands e5-reproduce, e5-discovery [--accept-deviation], e5-validation, each with --market IDX|US|CRYPTO, mirroring the e3/e4 blocks (lines 365-395): refuse a dirty idxsig/ tree, load the market's panel per protocol, stage directories created with exist_ok=False under research/E5/<market>/.

research/E5/protocol.json + PROTOCOL.md (frozen and committed before any flag or statistic; sha256 stamped into every stage output) with the detector definitions, plan grid, per-market harness blocks, periods, admissibility, selection, validation rule, consequence_if_failed ('the pre-spike tape family is exhausted on daily bars in that market; a further attempt is a new idea, not a re-tune'), and the declaration about 2023 re-use.

tests/test_e5.py: (1) flag equality of moonshot_e5.family_flags against an independent per-ticker loop implementation on a synthetic panel incl. zero-volume and missing-high/low rows; (2) A1_CREEP_QUIET on the pinned ZEAL.CO bars equals kod-machine price_facts.measures() facts at the four cutoffs (ties the harness rule to the frozen KOD definition); (3) prefix-first causality via rules.causal_signals on a random panel; (4) `python -m idxsig rules` audit passes; (5) e5.admissibility/select on a toy plans table; (6) Study runs with the E5 family on a global-v2-units panel.

Only after a market validates (out of scope of the experiment itself): paper.py _detector() hook for moonshot_e5 plus a new POLICY_ID (PAPER-POLICY-v5, prospective date) and a validation_evidence path for research/E5/<market>/validation; no change to PAPER-POLICY-v4 records.
result.falsifier: Kill result, per market, any of: (1) on discovery no member reaches 200 flags with an E30 Wilson lower bound above the base rate (the family carries no +30% information beyond chance, including the KOD VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET definition); (2) on discovery no (detector, plan) in the 24-pair grid has average net return > 0 with one-sided p < 0.05 against 200 matched random draws under the same plan AND positive average net in every discovery year with >= 50 scored (the structure detects but the flagged population's drift eats it, as with E1/E2); (3) the frozen pair's single 2023 validation run has scored < 100, average net <= 0, p >= 0.05 vs matched, or detection p >= 0.05 / lift <= 1. The exact result that kills the family outright: in all three markets the reference row A1_CREEP_QUIET|fixed1|fixed|h5 has average net return at or below the matched-random mean AND no pair is admissible on discovery; then pre-spike tape-only detection on daily bars is falsified for this lab across accumulation, re-base and contraction mechanisms, the KOD tape detector gets a negative population lift row, and the protocol's written consequence is that the next early-detection effort must use information inputs (filing acceptance times, catalyst calendars), not tape.
risks: Coverage: B1/B2 (a prior +30% day AND the re-base path) and C-members may produce fewer than 200 flags or 200 scored, especially on IDX (906 names) and crypto; reported in detector_selection.csv/plans.csv, never loosened after the fact.

Adverse population: the names most prone to +30% days have negative drift (US reverse-split/dilution names: 60% of E2 flags; IDX 'goreng' names with 0.55 untraded days in 20); a pre-spike flag may select them, giving E30 lift with negative average return ('detects but loses'); the per-year rule and matched controls make this visible rather than hiding it.

Repeat flags: creep and contraction persist for several sessions, so one name yields consecutive flags; overlap skip per name reduces scored trades at h10/h20 and detection precision counts ticker-days, so effective n is smaller than the flag count (reported).

Undefined features: IDX high/low missing on 12.5% of mirror rows and volume 0 on 12.5% make quiet/creep NaN (no flag) and bias coverage toward liquid names; crypto 24/7 sessions make rngr a UTC-day construct.

Multiplicity: 8 detectors and 24 pairs per market, 3 markets; p floor 0.005; mitigated by the per-year rule, the Wilson detection gate, one validation per market, and the full grid on record; a single market passing at p ~0.03 is weak evidence and the protocol says so.
2023 re-use: base-rate and big-day knowledge from E1/E2/E4 on 2023 is a declared leak; the pre-registration and the prospective paper arm are the mitigation, not a cure.

Fill models: IDX fill C can score infeasible entry-session fills (CORRECTION_01) and fill A/B are daily-bar proxies; a long hold (20) exits can roll over untraded/ARB-locked sessions; survivor-only US panel flatters longs.

Compute: 72 harness runs with 200 matched draws each, the US ones on a 4,878 x 1,006 panel, plus 24 Study.evaluate calls; the signal cache keyed by rule sha keeps signals to one computation per detector, but wall time is unmeasured (E3 ran 108 IDX runs; E4 288 crypto runs).

Expressibility on HEAD: stop_ref exits for US/crypto need PR #7's open-entry conditional machinery; on HEAD the grid is fixed-exit only for those markets; the choice must be fixed in protocol.json at freeze.

The hivol cross-sectional tercile depends on the listed universe at d; prefix-first checking guarantees causality but a US survivor universe shifts the tercile boundary relative to what was observable in real time.
result.directive_compliance: Holdout: the Study seals its market at the last validation session (e1.py:105-107) and every RunConfig sets end = 2023-12-29/31 explicitly; IDX runs touching 2024-01-02.. are refused by backtest.HOLDOUT; for US/crypto the protocol relies on explicit windows on HEAD and recommends merging PR #7 (clean merge-tree) first so GLOBAL_HOLDOUT refuses them in code; no holdout row is read, summarised or computed. No re-tune: no frozen detector (F1_ARA, G2_RET30, E3 candidates, E4 SELECTED) is touched or used as a candidate; the only prior-art definition reused (A1) was frozen 2026-10-08 for the Zealand card before any moonshot outcome was seen under it; all other thresholds are round numbers fixed in protocol.json before any flag is computed, and the admissibility/selection rules are copied from E1/E3 verbatim. No manufactured results: this proposal computes no statistic on any panel (no flag count, no return); every number will come from recorded harness runs (results/runs, RUNS.jsonl, write_run refusing a dirty tree) and Study outputs in append-only research/E5/<market>/ directories created with exist_ok=False; nothing historical is presented as prospective and the protocol's claims block says so. Pre-registration: protocol.json committed before the first run, sha256 stamped in reproduce/discovery/validation outputs; precondition reproduce stage first; SELECTED committed into the rule module before validation (hash covers the plan); one validation run per market; consequence_if_failed written in advance; the search size is visible in plans.csv and detector_selection.csv; read-only for this session (nothing created or run now).
result.expected_information_value: Either way the lab learns something it does not know: (1) the first population-level test of the KOD-DET-v0 tape detector VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET across ~1.4M eligible ticker-days in three markets, with base rate, precision, matched lift and non-events, which the KOD doctrine (lines 79-81) requires and which a single retrospective NO_SIGNAL card cannot give; (2) whether ANY pre-move tape structure on daily bars carries +30% information beyond the volatility/drawdown state, a question E1/E2's single-day weak signals at t-1 could not answer (they never measured multi-session creep, the quiet band, the re-base path or contraction); (3) a positive result in any market is the lab's first long detector whose entry precedes the move, with a validated executable plan that PAPER-POLICY-v5 could carry into the prospective ledger (today every paper decision is PASS because no (detector, plan) pair is validated); (4) a negative result in all three markets, written in advance as the consequence, closes the tape-only early-detection branch (accumulation, re-base, contraction) and justifies redirecting effort to information inputs with point-in-time timestamps (EDGAR acceptanceDateTime, Nasdaq Nordic releaseTime), which the data map identifies as the only unexplored dimension reachable for free; (5) the per-year and per-market tables show whether any effect is regime-bound (2021 hot years) as E3/E4 found, and the h5/h10/h20 comparison shows whether accumulation resolves on the 5-session horizon the whole lab has assumed.
